name: Visual Genome
description: A dataset of 108,249 images densely annotated with objects, attributes, relationships, region descriptions, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. Each image contains an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 relationships, 42 region descriptions, and 17 question-answer pairs. The dataset connects language and vision using crowdsourced annotations to enable comprehensive scene understanding and cognitive visual tasks.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei (Stanford University, Dresden University of Technology, Yahoo Inc., Snapchat Inc.)
citeAs: Ranjay Krishna et al. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1 [cs.CV] 23 Feb 2016
rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. The dataset uses 108,249 real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users. Region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, and question-answer pairs were collected through Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdsourcing tasks over 6 months.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from the intersection of YFCC100M (100 million Flickr images) and MS-COCO (328,000 images). The dataset contains 108,249 images ranging from 72 to 1280 pixels wide, with an average width of 500 pixels.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Objects from different region graphs that refer to the same object are merged if their bounding boxes have an overlap over union of 0.8. Workers confirm that pairs of objects with significant overlap are indeed the same object before merging. Region graphs are combined into scene graphs by merging co-referenced objects.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Region descriptions were preprocessed by lowercasing, lemmatizing, and stripping excess whitespace. BLEU score thresholds of 0.7 were used to ensure descriptions were dissimilar to both image-specific descriptions and the top 100 most common global descriptions. Stanford NLP tools were used to extract noun phrases from region descriptions and QAs. All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases were canonicalized to WordNet synsets using most frequent matching synsets with hand-crafted mapping rules for common failure cases.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers on Amazon Mechanical Turk were asked to: (1) draw bounding boxes and write descriptions for image regions, with explicit encouragement to write descriptions not previously written; (2) extract objects from descriptions and ground them with bounding boxes; (3) add attributes to objects or connect pairs of objects with relationships based on description text; (4) write question-answer pairs about images (freeform QAs) or based on given regions (region-based QAs), following rules to start with one of seven Ws (who, what, where, when, why, how, which) and avoid ambiguous questions. Workers were required to satisfy coverage (bounding box covers all mentioned objects) and quality (box as tight as possible, within 4 pixels) requirements. All annotations went through verification using majority voting (three workers vote, annotation added if at least two verify correctness) or rapid judgments for objects.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification conducted using two strategies: majority voting (three unique workers vote on each annotation, added to dataset if at least two verify correctness) and rapid judgments (for object verification only, using an interface inspired by rapid serial visual processing). Workers were shown top seven most similar descriptions using BLEU scores to prevent redundancy.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions (each with bounding box), 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs. For verification, three workers voted on each annotation using majority voting.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed from Amazon Mechanical Turk. Geographic distribution: 93.02% United States, 1.29% Philippines, 1.13% Kenya, 0.94% India, 0.50% Russia, 0.47% Canada, 2.65% others. Age distribution: majority between 25-34 years old, youngest 18 years old, oldest 68 years old. Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female. The dataset achieved a 94.1% retention rate.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP dependency parser and tools were used to automatically extract nouns and noun phrases as suggestions to speed up object extraction. VGG 16-layer network (Simonyan and Zisserman, 2014) was used to extract features for experiments. WordNet was used for canonicalization of objects, attributes, and relationships to synsets.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains human attributes including gender (man, woman), age-related attributes (young, old), and demographic descriptors. Annotator demographics were collected including age, gender, and geographic location.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as shown by the top synsets (ski, ballplayer, racket referring to people playing sports). Images are biased toward certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) due to source image distribution. The dataset uses images from Flickr which may not represent all visual contexts equally. Questions and answers follow a long-tail distribution common in QA datasets.
rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization to WordNet synsets is not perfect and contains some ambiguity. Mapping accuracy for objects is 86% with 98.5% recall, for attributes is 83.5% with 95.9% recall, and for relationships is 77.6% with 88.5% recall. WordNet's frequency counts prefer abstract senses over spatial senses present in visual data, requiring hand-crafted rules to correct common failure cases. The dataset's images are from Flickr and MS-COCO, which may limit generalization. Some region descriptions like 'it is a sunny day' contain no objects and have no region graphs. Relationships show high intra-class variability making them difficult to classify visually.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset enables training and benchmarking for comprehensive scene understanding tasks including: image description generation, visual question answering, object detection, attribute prediction, relationship prediction, semantic image retrieval, dense image captioning, relationship extraction, action recognition, and knowledge base construction. The dataset can be used for training, testing, and validation of computer vision models for both perceptual and cognitive tasks.
